# Dictate
A local-only push-to-talk dictation service. Its supported pipeline is:
``` press → in-memory microphone capture → local whisper.cpp → local Ollama cleanup → target revalidation → insert or recovery ```
It has no cloud fallback, telemetry, web service, GUI, database, clipboard fallback, or default content history.
## Requirements
- Python 3.11 or newer - The package dependencies installed from `pyproject.toml`: `sounddevice` and `pynput` - A locally installed `whisper.cpp` server and local speech model - [Ollama](https://ollama.com/) running locally with `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` acquired explicitly by the user - A microphone and platform permissions for microphone access, global keyboard monitoring, and verified text placement
Local runtime and model installation is a user-initiated setup operation. Normal dictation must work with the Internet disconnected after those local components are ready.
## Install
```bash python3 -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate python -m pip install -e . ollama pull qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M ```
Install `whisper.cpp` and its model using its local installation instructions, then start its loopback-only server. Do not configure either inference endpoint to a non-loopback address.
## Command contract
```bash dictate setup dictate devices dictate doctor dictate serve dictate serve --recover ```
- `setup` verifies the required local components and reports ready only when they are available. - `devices` lists local input identifiers and display names without recording. - `doctor` prints content-free readiness failures and platform-specific remediation. - `serve` runs the local push-to-talk pipeline. - `serve --recover` prints one pending in-process recovery result and immediately clears it. It does not use the clipboard and the result cannot survive process exit.
The command parser exposes this interface. The repository's acceptance tests exercise the service through deterministic local boundaries; connect a platform-specific verified-target adapter and local runtime boundaries before relying on ordinary `serve` operation on a desktop.
## Blessed defaults
A fresh configuration uses one supported pipeline:
| Setting | Default | |---|---| | Microphone | `system-default` | | Trigger | `right_alt` | | Style | `Natural` | | Local ASR endpoint | `http://127.0.0.1:8080` | | Local Ollama endpoint | `http://127.0.0.1:11434` | | Cleanup model | `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` | | Context limit | 1,024 characters |
The built-in cleanup styles are Natural, Formal, Casual, and Technical. Cleanup is mandatory, deterministic local Ollama processing; it transforms what was dictated and must not answer questions or add content.
## Privacy and safety
Audio, transcript, bounded destination context, dictionary terms, prompts, generated text, and a recovery result stay in memory for the active session. They are cleared after placement, failure, recovery consumption, timeout, or service exit. Ordinary logs and diagnostics contain status, timing, sizes, and error metadata only.
Both ASR and Ollama endpoints are validated as loopback-only before content can be sent. A remote endpoint is a hard configuration error, not a fallback choice.
Destination context is optional. If the platform cannot provide its bounded target-local context, diagnostics report the limitation and dictation proceeds without context. Screen capture, OCR, and collection from unrelated applications are not used.
Text is injected only after revalidating the original application, window, and text target captured at key-down. If that check fails, no destination receives text; use the explicit local recovery command instead.
## Platform behavior and validation
The cross-platform acceptance contract and the current content-free evidence are in [`specs/001-local-dictation/platform-acceptance-matrix.md`](specs/001-local-dictation/platform-acceptance-matrix.md). The generic key-monitoring path is shared. macOS, Windows, and Linux adapters fail closed for automatic placement until their platform has a verified original-target implementation; they report remediation rather than risking insertion into an unrelated field.
The warmed-model latency acceptance target is visible placement within five seconds of release for at least 90% of successful short dictations. The timing report carries only duration and outcome metadata.
## Validate
```bash PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v ```
The acceptance suite includes offline socket blocking, focus safety, privacy lifecycle checks, the common platform matrix, and a deterministic synthetic short-audio latency fixture.

# CLI Contract
## Commands
| Command | Contract | |---|---| | `dictate setup` | Verifies/assists explicit installation of local runtimes and models, selected/default microphone, trigger monitoring, text placement, and required context access. Reports ready only when all pass. Network use is permitted only for user-initiated installation/model acquisition. | | `dictate serve` | Starts the single long-running service. Defaults to OS microphone, platform-appropriate trigger, Natural style, local whisper.cpp, loopback Ollama, and no content history. Emits metadata-only status to stderr. | | `dictate doctor` | Executes real capability checks and prints actionable, platform-specific remediation without content. Exit nonzero when a required capability fails. | | `dictate devices` | Lists audio input identifiers and display names without recording content. |
## Exit and output rules
- Commands use stdout for requested data and stderr for status/errors. - Ordinary logs/output MUST NOT contain audio, transcript, context, prompt, or generated text. - `serve` does not expose an HTTP interface. - A non-loopback ASR/Ollama endpoint is a hard configuration error, never a fallback decision.
## Service event contract
`press`: snapshot target/context, then begin capture. `release`: stop capture and run local ASR then cleanup. Insert only after exact target revalidation. On focus mismatch retain an in-memory recovery result; on ASR or cleanup failure discard content and report only a content-free actionable error.

# Platform Acceptance Matrix
This matrix defines the same observable contract on macOS, Windows, and Linux. The implementation may use different native mechanisms only when the generic `pynput` route is demonstrably insufficient. Every diagnostic and evidence record is metadata-only: it must never contain audio, transcript, context, prompts, dictionary entries, or generated text.
## Required matrix
| Capability | macOS | Windows | Linux | Common acceptance result | |---|---|---|---|---| | Trigger | Generic held-key monitoring | Generic held-key monitoring | Generic held-key monitoring | Key-down begins one session; matching key-up releases it; repeated key-down does not duplicate a session. | | Microphone | OS default or selected input | OS default or selected input | OS default or selected input | A missing, disconnected, or unavailable input is a content-free readiness failure before recording. | | Permissions | Microphone and Accessibility remediation | Microphone/input and accessibility remediation | Microphone/input and desktop-accessibility remediation | Required permission failure is nonzero/not-ready and names an OS-appropriate remedy without user content. | | Destination context | Optional Accessibility-backed context | Optional accessibility-backed context | Optional desktop-accessibility-backed context | Its absence is a limitation, never a block to ordinary context-free dictation and never a reason to broaden collection. | | Target safety | Original application/window/text target | Original application/window/text target | Original application/window/text target | Snapshot at key-down; exact revalidation immediately before insertion; any mismatch inserts nowhere. | | Insertion/recovery | Direct injection only after verification | Direct injection only after verification | Direct injection only after verification | Verification or insertion failure retains one in-process recovery result only; no clipboard or file fallback. | | Diagnostics | `setup`/`doctor` remediation | `setup`/`doctor` remediation | `setup`/`doctor` remediation | Content-free required failures and optional limitations; no cloud fallback. |
## Current evidence — 2026-08-11
| Platform | Trigger contract | Microphone/permission diagnostics | Optional context | Target safety/insertion/recovery | Evidence | Result | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | macOS | Generic hotkey adapter is instantiable | Reports remediation when target verification/accessibility is unavailable | Reported as non-blocking limitation | Fails closed: no target snapshot and no insertion until a verified target mechanism exists; recovery instruction is available | `tests.unit.test_platform_adapters`; `tests.acceptance.test_platform_matrix` | PASS for safe common contract; automatic placement intentionally unavailable pending verified native evidence | | Windows | Generic hotkey adapter is instantiable | Reports remediation when target verification is unavailable | Reported as non-blocking limitation | Fails closed: no target snapshot and no insertion until a verified target mechanism exists; recovery instruction is available | `tests.unit.test_platform_adapters`; `tests.acceptance.test_platform_matrix` | PASS for safe common contract; automatic placement intentionally unavailable pending Windows-host validation | | Linux | Generic hotkey adapter is instantiable | Reports desktop-session remediation when target verification is unavailable | Reported as non-blocking limitation | Fails closed: no target snapshot and no insertion until a verified target mechanism exists; recovery instruction is available | `tests.unit.test_platform_adapters`; `tests.acceptance.test_platform_matrix` | PASS for safe common contract; automatic placement intentionally unavailable pending Linux desktop-session validation |
The matrix test runs the same press/release, optional-context, focus-change, no-insertion, and memory-only recovery contract for every row. It uses deterministic non-user data and does not need local models, a microphone, or an external network connection.
## Warmed-model latency acceptance
Use the fixed 100 ms, 16 kHz mono signed-16-bit silence fixture in `tests/acceptance/test_platform_matrix.py`; it is deterministic synthetic data, not captured user audio. Start the resident local whisper.cpp process and warm the configured Ollama model via its local readiness request before timed runs. For each platform, perform 20 short dictations against a verified supported text target.
- Start the monotonic clock on trigger release. - Stop it when verified insertion returns visible placement. - Record only `platform`, sample number, duration in milliseconds, outcome category, and pass/fail. - A successful sample passes only when it is visible within 5,000 ms. - The platform passes when at least 90% of successful short samples pass. Failures remain content-free diagnostic outcomes and do not become cloud retries.
`PlacementTiming` and `tests.acceptance.test_latency` provide the release-to-placement clock seam and enforce the five-second threshold without recording content. Real-device results must be stored only as content-free project evidence, if retained at all.

# Feature Specification: Local Push-to-Talk Dictation
**Feature Branch**: `001-local-dictation`
**Created**: 2026-08-11
**Status**: Draft
**Input**: User description: "Build a privacy-first, cross-platform local dictation tool that behaves like a system-wide push-to-talk writing assistant."
## Clarifications
### Session 2026-08-11
- Q: When focus changes after dictation begins, when may the service automatically insert the completed text? → A: Insert only if the original application, window, and text target can still be verified immediately before insertion; otherwise do not insert and retain a local recovery result. - Q: If local speech recognition or cleanup fails, what should happen to the audio-derived result? → A: Discard audio and unusable intermediate content, insert nothing, and report a content-free actionable failure. - Q: What local destination context may be collected for a dictation session? → A: Collect only active application identity, active window/document identity, current selection, and a bounded nearby-text excerpt from the same original target; otherwise collect no context. - Q: If the same spoken term has different spellings in the global and applicable project-specific dictionaries, which spelling takes precedence? → A: The applicable project-specific entry takes precedence for that dictation session; otherwise use the global entry. - Q: When guided setup finishes, what must be true before it may report success? → A: All capabilities required: local processing, microphone, global trigger monitoring, safe text placement, and destination-context access are verified; otherwise setup provides platform-appropriate remediation and does not report success.
## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
### User Story 1 - Dictate into the Active Field (Priority: P1)
A user starts the dictation service, focuses a text field in any supported application, holds the configured global push-to-talk trigger while speaking, and releases it. The user receives polished text in the same field without manually handling audio, a transcript, or a clipboard.
**Why this priority**: This is the primary product experience and independently delivers the core value of hands-free local writing assistance.
**Independent Test**: With the service running and no network connection, hold and release the trigger while a supported text field remains active; verify that the final text appears in that field and no copy/paste step is needed.
**Acceptance Scenarios**:
1. **Given** the service is ready and a supported text field has focus, **When** the user holds the configured global trigger, speaks, and releases it, **Then** recording starts on key-down, ends on key-up, processing starts automatically, and polished text is placed in the original field. 2. **Given** the user has no network connection, **When** they complete a normal dictation, **Then** the dictation completes locally without a cloud fallback or a network requirement. 3. **Given** the configured trigger conflicts with platform behavior or is unavailable, **When** the user starts the service, **Then** the service explains the issue and does not record until a usable trigger is configured.
---
### User Story 2 - Trust Local Privacy (Priority: P1)
A privacy-conscious user can dictate sensitive content knowing that audio, transcripts, destination context, cleanup instructions, and generated text remain on the computer and are not retained by default.
**Why this priority**: Privacy and offline operation are non-negotiable product promises; without them the product does not meet its purpose.
**Independent Test**: Perform a representative dictation while offline, inspect ordinary logs and application-managed storage, and verify that dictated and contextual test content is absent.
**Acceptance Scenarios**:
1. **Given** the user dictates content containing a unique sensitive phrase, **When** processing finishes, **Then** the phrase is absent from ordinary operational logs and default persistent artifacts. 2. **Given** a network connection becomes unavailable during normal use, **When** the user dictates, **Then** the service continues its local workflow or reports a local-component failure without sending content or attempting a cloud fallback. 3. **Given** the service gathers destination context, **When** it prepares cleanup, **Then** it uses only bounded information related to the active target and keeps that information local.
---
### User Story 3 - Produce Faithful Polished Writing (Priority: P1)
A user dictates natural speech and receives readable prose with appropriate punctuation, capitalization, paragraphs, and lists. The service removes ordinary filler and resolves explicit false starts or self-corrections while retaining the meaning of what the user said.
**Why this priority**: Raw transcription alone does not deliver the promised writing-assistant experience; faithful cleanup is essential to its value and safety.
**Independent Test**: Dictate a scripted sample with filler, an explicit correction, a list, and a question; compare the output to the expected written form and verify that it neither answers the question nor adds unsupported facts.
**Acceptance Scenarios**:
1. **Given** a dictation includes ordinary filler and an explicit self-correction, **When** cleanup completes, **Then** the resulting text omits the filler and reflects the corrected intent. 2. **Given** a user dictates a question, **When** cleanup completes, **Then** the output renders the dictated question but does not answer it. 3. **Given** a user selects a built-in writing style, **When** cleanup completes, **Then** style changes formatting and tone without changing substantive meaning or adding facts.
---
### User Story 4 - Use Local Vocabulary and Target Context (Priority: P2)
A user maintains directly editable local vocabulary for names, product terms, technical terms, identifiers, acronyms, and project-specific words. The user can dictate into a relevant destination and benefit from bounded local destination context and applicable vocabulary without exposing either outside the computer.
**Why this priority**: Accurate terminology and appropriately formatted output materially improve usefulness for professional dictation while preserving the privacy promise.
**Independent Test**: Add distinctive terms to global and project-specific dictionaries, dictate a sample into a matching project destination, and verify their expected spellings are present in the final local output.
**Acceptance Scenarios**:
1. **Given** a term appears in the user's local dictionary, **When** the user dictates that term, **Then** the final text uses the known spelling when the spoken input reasonably matches it. 2. **Given** a project-specific dictionary applies to the active target, **When** the user dictates, **Then** applicable project terms supplement rather than replace global dictionary terms. 3. **Given** destination-context access is unavailable or permission is denied, **When** the user runs setup, **Then** setup does not report success, does not broaden collection, and provides platform-appropriate remediation instructions.
---
### User Story 5 - Set Up and Diagnose the Service (Priority: P2)
A new user can run a guided command-line setup that checks local prerequisites, permissions, audio input, and local processing. The user can list microphones, select a non-default device when needed, and run diagnostics that explain failures without revealing dictated content.
**Why this priority**: A system-wide service needs clear installation, permissions, and recovery paths before it can provide reliable daily use across supported operating systems.
**Independent Test**: On each supported operating system, complete setup using the default microphone, then run device inspection and diagnostics with a deliberately unavailable microphone or denied permission; verify actionable, content-free results.
**Acceptance Scenarios**:
1. **Given** a first-time user, **When** they run setup, **Then** it guides them through verifying required local components, local processing, microphone access, and keyboard capabilities with platform-appropriate permission guidance. 2. **Given** the operating system default microphone is available, **When** the user starts normal dictation without selecting a device, **Then** recording uses that microphone. 3. **Given** a selected microphone becomes unavailable, **When** dictation begins, **Then** recording is not started and the user receives an understandable device-specific failure.
---
### User Story 6 - Prevent Misplaced Sensitive Text (Priority: P2)
A user begins dictation in one field but changes focus before processing finishes. The service avoids typing confidential output into an unrelated destination and gives the user a deliberate, local way to recover the result when safe placement cannot be confirmed.
**Why this priority**: Safe placement is necessary to protect privacy when system focus changes during asynchronous processing.
**Independent Test**: Start dictation in one supported field, change focus to a different field before processing completes, and verify that generated text is not silently typed into the new field and is available for explicit recovery.
**Acceptance Scenarios**:
1. **Given** the original application, window, and text target can still be verified immediately before placement, **When** processing completes, **Then** the final text is inserted into that original target. 2. **Given** focus changes and safe placement cannot be determined, **When** processing completes, **Then** the service does not type into the new target and preserves the result only for explicit local recovery.
### Edge Cases
- The user releases the trigger before meaningful audio is captured; the service reports no usable dictation and inserts nothing. - Microphone permission, keyboard monitoring, or text-placement permission is denied, revoked, or unavailable; the service explains the affected capability and does not silently degrade privacy. - The selected or default microphone is disconnected during recording; recording ends safely and the user receives an understandable failure without retaining partial audio by default. - Local recognition or cleanup is unavailable, fails, or produces no usable result; the service discards captured audio and unusable intermediate content, sends no data externally, inserts nothing, and provides a content-free actionable failure. - The active application does not expose usable target identity or does not support text placement; the service does not broaden context collection and offers explicit local recovery where a result exists. - A dictionary entry is malformed or duplicated; the service identifies the local configuration issue without corrupting either dictionary. A spelling conflict between an applicable project-specific entry and a global entry uses the project-specific spelling for that session. - The user changes writing style, microphone, or trigger while a dictation is in progress; the active dictation completes or fails under its starting settings, and the new setting applies to later use.
## Requirements *(mandatory)*
### Functional Requirements
- **FR-001**: The system MUST provide a long-running command-line dictation service as the primary user interface, plus command-line setup, diagnostics, audio-input inspection, and configuration operations; it MUST NOT require a graphical interface. - **FR-002**: The system MUST support normal dictation on macOS, Windows, and Linux, with a platform-independent core workflow and platform-appropriate behavior for system integration. - **FR-003**: The system MUST let users configure a globally usable push-to-talk trigger and MAY use platform-specific defaults where necessary. - **FR-004**: The system MUST start recording on trigger key-down, stop recording on key-up, and begin local processing automatically after key-up. - **FR-005**: The system MUST use the operating system's default available microphone without required configuration and MUST let users select an available audio input explicitly. - **FR-006**: The system MUST provide a command that lists available audio inputs and MUST report an understandable failure when the selected or default input is unavailable or disconnected. - **FR-007**: The system MUST recognize speech locally and transform the resulting transcript locally into polished written text as one supported default pipeline. - **FR-008**: Normal dictation MUST function without Internet access. The system MUST NOT send speech audio, transcripts, destination context, dictionary contents, cleanup instructions, generated text, or derived user content outside the local computer, and MUST NOT use an automatic cloud fallback. - **FR-009**: By default, the system MUST treat captured audio, transcripts, destination context, cleanup instructions, generated text, and dictation history as ephemeral. It MUST NOT maintain history of audio, transcripts, or cleanup inputs and outputs. - **FR-010**: The system MUST NOT write user content to ordinary logs. Operational logging MAY include only timing, status, sizes, and error metadata. - **FR-011**: The system MUST offer built-in Natural, Formal, Casual, and Technical writing styles, select Natural by default, and apply style only to cleanup and formatting rather than substantive meaning. - **FR-012**: Cleanup MUST preserve the user's intended meaning; it MAY remove ordinary filler and resolve explicit false starts or self-corrections, and it MUST apply appropriate punctuation, capitalization, paragraphing, and list formatting when supported by the dictated content. - **FR-013**: Cleanup MUST NOT answer dictated questions, invent facts, add substantive content, or alter supplied terminology beyond formatting necessary for the selected writing style. - **FR-014**: The system MUST provide directly user-editable local global dictionary data for known names, product terms, technical terms, identifiers, acronyms, and project-specific vocabulary. - **FR-015**: The system MUST allow applicable project-specific vocabulary to supplement the global dictionary without replacing or modifying it, and MUST use known spellings to improve final transcription. When an applicable project-specific entry conflicts with a global entry, the project-specific spelling MUST take precedence for that dictation session. - **FR-016**: The system MAY collect local destination context only from the original dictation target and only when that target and required permission are available. It MUST be limited to active application identity, active window/document identity, the current selection, and a bounded nearby-text excerpt from that same target; it MUST otherwise collect no context. Collected context MUST remain local and ephemeral by default and MUST NOT use screen capture, OCR, or unrelated applications. - **FR-017**: The system MUST insert completed text without a separate copy/paste workflow only when the original application, window, and text target can still be verified immediately before placement. - **FR-018**: If the original application, window, or text target cannot be verified immediately before placement, including because focus changed, the system MUST NOT insert text into any destination and MUST preserve any generated result only for explicit local user recovery. - **FR-019**: Setup MUST report success only after it verifies required local components and models, local processing, a usable microphone, global trigger monitoring, safe text-placement capability, and destination-context access. If any required capability is unavailable, setup MUST NOT report success and MUST provide platform-appropriate remediation instructions. - **FR-020**: Diagnostics MUST report actionable readiness and failure information without exposing audio, transcripts, destination context, cleanup instructions, or generated text. - **FR-021**: The system MUST preserve normal dictation privacy and local-only behavior when a permission, device, recognition, cleanup, context, or placement operation fails; it MUST provide a content-free, understandable failure rather than disclose content or fall back to a network service. When recognition or cleanup fails or yields no usable result, it MUST discard captured audio and unusable intermediate content and MUST insert nothing.
### Key Entities *(include if feature involves data)*
- **Dictation session**: An ephemeral interaction beginning at trigger key-down and ending after final text is safely placed, explicitly recoverable, or discarded; includes the original target identity and status but does not imply default persistent history. - **Audio input preference**: The user's choice of default-system or explicitly selected microphone, together with availability status. - **Push-to-talk preference**: The globally monitored trigger and its platform-specific availability status. - **Writing style**: A selected local cleanup and formatting preference; built-in values are Natural, Formal, Casual, and Technical. - **Global dictionary**: Directly editable local vocabulary that applies to the user's dictation. - **Project dictionary**: Directly editable local vocabulary associated with a relevant project or target that supplements global vocabulary. - **Destination context**: Bounded, ephemeral local information about the active dictation target used only to improve recognition and formatting. - **Recovery result**: Locally retained generated text awaiting an explicit user action after safe automatic placement could not be determined. - **Diagnostic result**: Content-free status and actionable remediation information for prerequisites, permissions, audio inputs, keyboard integration, local processing, and placement capability.
## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*
### Measurable Outcomes
- **SC-001**: In an offline acceptance test with all required local components ready, a user completes 95% of 20 scripted push-to-talk dictations from key-down through final text placement without a manual copy/paste step. - **SC-002**: In the same offline test, at least 90% of successful short dictations produce final text within 5 seconds of trigger release, measured from the user's release to visible placement. - **SC-003**: For a scripted set of 20 samples containing filler, explicit corrections, questions, terminology, paragraphs, and lists, reviewers confirm that 100% of outputs do not answer dictated questions or introduce unsupported substantive facts. - **SC-004**: In privacy regression tests containing unique audio-derived, contextual, and generated markers, 100% of inspected ordinary logs and default persistent artifacts contain none of those markers. - **SC-005**: In 20 focus-change tests where safe placement cannot be confirmed, 100% of generated results are withheld from the newly focused unrelated field and made available only through explicit local recovery. - **SC-006**: On macOS, Windows, and Linux, a new user can complete guided setup, identify an available microphone, and obtain an actionable diagnostic result for a denied permission or unavailable device without exposing user content.
## Assumptions
- The first release supports one active dictation session at a time and targets text fields in applications that allow the operating system's supported text-placement mechanisms. - Normal operation has all required local components and models installed during explicit setup or update; obtaining them may require network access only when the user explicitly initiates it. - Natural is the default style; built-in styles are available immediately, while user-defined custom styles are a future extension and are not required for this feature. - The default microphone is the operating-system default at the start of a session. An explicit device selection is retained as a user preference without retaining dictated content. - Local recovery is an explicit, user-controlled action and is designed to avoid placing generated text into an unrelated field; its precise interaction is deferred to planning as long as it remains command-line compatible and local-only. - Destination-context access is a required first-run readiness capability. Setup does not report success when it is unavailable, unsupported, or denied; it provides platform-appropriate remediation instead and does not broaden collection to compensate. - The stated success-criterion sample sizes and latency target are initial acceptance thresholds that may be refined during planning only if privacy, correctness, and offline operation are preserved.

**Why this priority**: Raw transcription alone does not deliver the promised writing-assistant experience; faithful cleanup is essential to its value and safety.
**Independent Test**: Dictate a scripted sample with filler, an explicit correction, a list, and a question; compare the output to the expected written form and verify that it neither answers the question nor adds unsupported facts.
**Acceptance Scenarios**:
1. **Given** a dictation includes ordinary filler and an explicit self-correction, **When** cleanup completes, **Then** the resulting text omits the filler and reflects the corrected intent. 2. **Given** a user dictates a question, **When** cleanup completes, **Then** the output renders the dictated question but does not answer it. 3. **Given** a user selects a built-in writing style, **When** cleanup completes, **Then** style changes formatting and tone without changing substantive meaning or adding facts.
---
### User Story 4 - Use Local Vocabulary and Target Context (Priority: P2)
A user maintains directly editable local vocabulary for names, product terms, technical terms, identifiers, acronyms, and project-specific words. The user can dictate into a relevant destination and benefit from bounded local destination context and applicable vocabulary without exposing either outside the computer.
**Why this priority**: Accurate terminology and appropriately formatted output materially improve usefulness for professional dictation while preserving the privacy promise.
**Independent Test**: Add distinctive terms to global and project-specific dictionaries, dictate a sample into a matching project destination, and verify their expected spellings are present in the final local output.
**Acceptance Scenarios**:
1. **Given** a term appears in the user's local dictionary, **When** the user dictates that term, **Then** the final text uses the known spelling when the spoken input reasonably matches it. 2. **Given** a project-specific dictionary applies to the active target, **When** the user dictates, **Then** applicable project terms supplement rather than replace global dictionary terms. 3. **Given** destination-context access is unavailable or permission is denied, **When** the user runs setup, **Then** setup reports the limited enhancement and remediation, does not broaden collection, and normal dictation remains available without context.
---
### User Story 5 - Set Up and Diagnose the Service (Priority: P2)
A new user can run a guided command-line setup that checks local prerequisites, permissions, audio input, and local processing. The user can list microphones, select a non-default device when needed, and run diagnostics that explain failures without revealing dictated content.
**Why this priority**: A system-wide service needs clear installation, permissions, and recovery paths before it can provide reliable daily use across supported operating systems.
**Independent Test**: On each supported operating system, complete setup using the default microphone, then run device inspection and diagnostics with a deliberately unavailable microphone or denied permission; verify actionable, content-free results.
**Acceptance Scenarios**:
1. **Given** a first-time user, **When** they run setup, **Then** it guides them through verifying required local components, local processing, microphone access, and keyboard capabilities with platform-appropriate permission guidance. 2. **Given** the operating system default microphone is available, **When** the user starts normal dictation without selecting a device, **Then** recording uses that microphone. 3. **Given** a selected microphone becomes unavailable, **When** dictation begins, **Then** recording is not started and the user receives an understandable device-specific failure.
---
### User Story 6 - Prevent Misplaced Sensitive Text (Priority: P2)
A user begins dictation in one field but changes focus before processing finishes. The service avoids typing confidential output into an unrelated destination and gives the user a deliberate, local way to recover the result when safe placement cannot be confirmed.
**Why this priority**: Safe placement is necessary to protect privacy when system focus changes during asynchronous processing.
**Independent Test**: Start dictation in one supported field, change focus to a different field before processing completes, and verify that generated text is not silently typed into the new field and is available for explicit recovery.
**Acceptance Scenarios**:
1. **Given** the original application, window, and text target can still be verified immediately before placement, **When** processing completes, **Then** the final text is inserted into that original target. 2. **Given** focus changes and safe placement cannot be determined, **When** processing completes, **Then** the service does not type into the new target and preserves the result only for explicit local recovery.
### Edge Cases
- The user releases the trigger before meaningful audio is captured; the service reports no usable dictation and inserts nothing. - Microphone permission, keyboard monitoring, or text-placement permission is denied, revoked, or unavailable; the service explains the affected capability and does not silently degrade privacy. - The selected or default microphone is disconnected during recording; recording ends safely and the user receives an understandable failure without retaining partial audio by default. - Local recognition or cleanup is unavailable, fails, or produces no usable result; the service discards captured audio and unusable intermediate content, sends no data externally, inserts nothing, and provides a content-free actionable failure. - The active application does not expose usable target identity or does not support text placement; the service does not broaden context collection and offers explicit local recovery where a result exists. - A dictionary entry is malformed or duplicated; the service identifies the local configuration issue without corrupting either dictionary. A spelling conflict between an applicable project-specific entry and a global entry uses the project-specific spelling for that session. - The user changes writing style, microphone, or trigger while a dictation is in progress; the active dictation completes or fails under its starting settings, and the new setting applies to later use.
## Requirements *(mandatory)*
### Functional Requirements
- **FR-001**: The system MUST provide a long-running command-line dictation service as the primary user interface, plus command-line setup, diagnostics, audio-input inspection, and configuration operations; it MUST NOT require a graphical interface. - **FR-002**: The system MUST support normal dictation on macOS, Windows, and Linux, with a platform-independent core workflow and platform-appropriate behavior for system integration. - **FR-003**: The system MUST let users configure a globally usable push-to-talk trigger and MAY use platform-specific defaults where necessary. - **FR-004**: The system MUST start recording on trigger key-down, stop recording on key-up, and begin local processing automatically after key-up. - **FR-005**: The system MUST use the operating system's default available microphone without required configuration and MUST let users select an available audio input explicitly. - **FR-006**: The system MUST provide a command that lists available audio inputs and MUST report an understandable failure when the selected or default input is unavailable or disconnected. - **FR-007**: The system MUST recognize speech locally and transform the resulting transcript locally into polished written text as one supported default pipeline. - **FR-008**: Normal dictation MUST function without Internet access. The system MUST NOT send speech audio, transcripts, destination context, dictionary contents, cleanup instructions, generated text, or derived user content outside the local computer, and MUST NOT use an automatic cloud fallback. - **FR-009**: By default, the system MUST treat captured audio, transcripts, destination context, cleanup instructions, generated text, and dictation history as ephemeral. It MUST NOT maintain history of audio, transcripts, or cleanup inputs and outputs. - **FR-010**: The system MUST NOT write user content to ordinary logs. Operational logging MAY include only timing, status, sizes, and error metadata. - **FR-011**: The system MUST offer built-in Natural, Formal, Casual, and Technical writing styles, select Natural by default, and apply style only to cleanup and formatting rather than substantive meaning. - **FR-012**: Cleanup MUST preserve the user's intended meaning; it MAY remove ordinary filler and resolve explicit false starts or self-corrections, and it MUST apply appropriate punctuation, capitalization, paragraphing, and list formatting when supported by the dictated content. - **FR-013**: Cleanup MUST NOT answer dictated questions, invent facts, add substantive content, or alter supplied terminology beyond formatting necessary for the selected writing style. - **FR-014**: The system MUST provide directly user-editable local global dictionary data for known names, product terms, technical terms, identifiers, acronyms, and project-specific vocabulary. - **FR-015**: The system MUST allow applicable project-specific vocabulary to supplement the global dictionary without replacing or modifying it, and MUST use known spellings to improve final transcription. When an applicable project-specific entry conflicts with a global entry, the project-specific spelling MUST take precedence for that dictation session. - **FR-016**: The system MAY collect local destination context only from the original dictation target and only when that target and required permission are available. It MUST be limited to active application identity, active window/document identity, the current selection, and a bounded nearby-text excerpt from that same target; it MUST otherwise collect no context. Collected context MUST remain local and ephemeral by default and MUST NOT use screen capture, OCR, or unrelated applications. - **FR-017**: The system MUST insert completed text without a separate copy/paste workflow only when the original application, window, and text target can still be verified immediately before placement. - **FR-018**: If the original application, window, or text target cannot be verified immediately before placement, including because focus changed, the system MUST NOT insert text into any destination and MUST preserve any generated result only for explicit local user recovery. - **FR-019**: Setup MUST report success only after it verifies required local components and models, local processing, a usable microphone, global trigger monitoring, and safe text-placement capability. Destination-context access is optional: if unavailable, setup MUST report the limitation and platform-appropriate remediation without preventing normal dictation without context. - **FR-020**: Diagnostics MUST report actionable readiness and failure information without exposing audio, transcripts, destination context, cleanup instructions, or generated text. - **FR-021**: The system MUST preserve normal dictation privacy and local-only behavior when a permission, device, recognition, cleanup, context, or placement operation fails; it MUST provide a content-free, understandable failure rather than disclose content or fall back to a network service. When recognition or cleanup fails or yields no usable result, it MUST discard captured audio and unusable intermediate content and MUST insert nothing.
### Key Entities *(include if feature involves data)*
- **Dictation session**: An ephemeral interaction beginning at trigger key-down and ending after final text is safely placed, explicitly recoverable, or discarded; includes the original target identity and status but does not imply default persistent history. - **Audio input preference**: The user's choice of default-system or explicitly selected microphone, together with availability status. - **Push-to-talk preference**: The globally monitored trigger and its platform-specific availability status. - **Writing style**: A selected local cleanup and formatting preference; built-in values are Natural, Formal, Casual, and Technical. - **Global dictionary**: Directly editable local vocabulary that applies to the user's dictation. - **Project dictionary**: Directly editable local vocabulary associated with a relevant project or target that supplements global vocabulary. - **Destination context**: Bounded, ephemeral local information about the active dictation target used only to improve recognition and formatting. - **Recovery result**: Locally retained generated text awaiting an explicit user action after safe automatic placement could not be determined. - **Diagnostic result**: Content-free status and actionable remediation information for prerequisites, permissions, audio inputs, keyboard integration, local processing, and placement capability.
## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*
### Measurable Outcomes
- **SC-001**: In an offline acceptance test with all required local components ready, a user completes 95% of 20 scripted push-to-talk dictations from key-down through final text placement without a manual copy/paste step. - **SC-002**: In the same offline test, at least 90% of successful short dictations produce final text within 5 seconds of trigger release, measured from the user's release to visible placement. - **SC-003**: For a scripted set of 20 samples containing filler, explicit corrections, questions, terminology, paragraphs, and lists, reviewers confirm that 100% of outputs do not answer dictated questions or introduce unsupported substantive facts. - **SC-004**: In privacy regression tests containing unique audio-derived, contextual, and generated markers, 100% of inspected ordinary logs and default persistent artifacts contain none of those markers. - **SC-005**: In 20 focus-change tests where safe placement cannot be confirmed, 100% of generated results are withheld from the newly focused unrelated field and made available only through explicit local recovery. - **SC-006**: On macOS, Windows, and Linux, a new user can complete guided setup, identify an available microphone, and obtain an actionable diagnostic result for a denied permission or unavailable device without exposing user content.
## Assumptions
- The first release supports one active dictation session at a time and targets text fields in applications that allow the operating system's supported text-placement mechanisms. - Normal operation has all required local components and models installed during explicit setup or update; obtaining them may require network access only when the user explicitly initiates it. - Natural is the default style; built-in styles are available immediately, while user-defined custom styles are a future extension and are not required for this feature. - The default microphone is the operating-system default at the start of a session. An explicit device selection is retained as a user preference without retaining dictated content. - Local recovery is an explicit, user-controlled action and is designed to avoid placing generated text into an unrelated field; its precise interaction is deferred to planning as long as it remains command-line compatible and local-only. - Destination-context access is an optional enhancement. When it is unavailable, unsupported, or denied, setup reports platform-appropriate remediation, normal dictation continues without context, and the service does not broaden collection to compensate. - The stated success-criterion sample sizes and latency target are initial acceptance thresholds that may be refined during planning only if privacy, correctness, and offline operation are preserved.

# Tasks: Local Push-to-Talk Dictation
**Input**: `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `research.md`, `data-model.md`, `contracts/cli.md`, and `quickstart.md`
## Dependencies
`Setup → foundations/readiness → complete safe local pipeline → privacy/fidelity → dictionary → setup/devices/context → styles → platform matrix → polish`.
## Phase 1: Setup and Foundations
- [X] T001 Create `pyproject.toml` for Python 3.11+ with only `sounddevice` and `pynput`; `python -m dictate --help` exposes `setup`, `serve`, `doctor`, and `devices`. - [X] T002 Create the package/test skeleton described in `plan.md`; `unittest` discovers an empty passing suite. - [X] T003 Implement TOML defaults, text dictionaries, atomic preference writes, and state transitions; unit tests prove Natural/default microphone/default trigger selection and content clearing on every terminal state. - [X] T004 Implement shared readiness checks for local runtimes/models, microphone, trigger, placement, and optional context capability; unit tests distinguish required readiness failure from non-blocking context limitation. - [X] T005 Implement loopback-only endpoint validation and metadata-only logging; unit tests prove non-loopback inference is rejected before content can be sent. - [X] T006 Define the narrow platform adapter contract for target snapshots, optional context, permissions, hotkeys, insertion, and explicit recovery.
## Phase 2: P1 Complete Safe Local Dictation Slice
**Goal**: Prove press → target snapshot → in-memory audio → local ASR → local Ollama cleanup → target revalidation → insert or explicit recovery.
- [X] T007 Implement default-microphone in-memory PCM capture and press/release lifecycle; unit tests prove press starts capture, release stops it, and empty capture inserts nothing. - [X] T008 Implement supervised loopback whisper-server with resident model and memory-backed ASR submission; integration tests prove readiness, successful local transcription, and content-free local failure. - [X] T009 Implement loopback Ollama cleanup using the blessed model, `think: false`, deterministic options, bounded context, keep-alive, and output-only validation; integration tests prove transformed text is returned and no answer is generated. - [X] T010 Implement generic `pynput` press/release monitoring, target snapshot, target revalidation, and injection; unit tests prove an unverified target never receives injected text. - [X] T011 Implement in-process recovery: on unsafe placement retain one final result for `dictate serve --recover` to print once to stdout, clear it immediately after read/timeout/exit, and never use clipboard; acceptance tests prove this lifecycle. - [X] T012 Wire `dictate serve` through the complete pipeline with an intentionally empty dictionary in this first slice; integration tests prove ASR and Ollama are both mandatory stages. - [X] T013 Add focus-change acceptance coverage: begin in target A, change to B, prove B receives no text and recovery is required. - [X] T014 Add an observable offline end-to-end acceptance harness that blocks all non-loopback socket connections for the service process while allowing required loopback runtimes; prove the full pipeline still inserts output.
## Phase 3: Privacy and Faithful Cleanup
- [X] T015 Add fixed cleanup corpus and regression tests for filler, false starts, terms, questions, lists, and all styles; expected outputs preserve meaning and never answer or invent content. - [X] T016 Add privacy regressions with unique sentinels for transcript, context, dictionary terms, prompt, output, and recovery result; inspect logs, config, temp locations, and artifacts after success/failure/cancellation and prove no sentinel persists. - [X] T017 [Conditional] Only if memory-backed whisper submission is proven unavailable, implement restrictive temporary-audio creation/deletion; tests prove deletion after success, ASR failure, cancellation, and process interruption. Otherwise document that no temporary-audio path exists.
## Phase 4: P2 Dictionary, Devices, Setup, Context, Styles
- [X] T018 Implement global/project dictionary discovery and project-over-global precedence; unit tests prove dictionary terms reach both supported ASR prompting and cleanup prompt construction. - [X] T019 Implement `setup`, `doctor`, and `devices` using shared readiness checks; command tests prove required failures are nonzero, optional context is a non-blocking limitation, and remediation is content-free. - [X] T020 Implement explicit microphone selection and unavailable/disconnected/default-change failures; integration tests prove clear failure before recording. - [X] T021 Implement bounded original-target context and permission handling; unit tests prove only allowed fields are collected and unavailable context does not block dictation. - [X] T022 Implement Natural/Formal/Casual/Technical profiles; prompt tests prove style changes do not change substantive meaning.
## Phase 5: Platform Matrix, Latency, and Polish
- [ ] T023 Define the shared macOS/Windows/Linux acceptance matrix for trigger, microphone, permissions, optional context, target safety, insertion/recovery, and diagnostics; it permits different low-level implementations. - [ ] T024 Validate macOS against the matrix and implement only required macOS adapter refinements; record pass/fail evidence without content. - [ ] T025 Validate Windows against the matrix and implement only required Windows adapter refinements; record pass/fail evidence without content. - [ ] T026 Validate Linux against the matrix and implement only required Linux adapter refinements; record pass/fail evidence without content. - [ ] T027 Add warmed-model latency acceptance fixtures: fixed short audio, release-to-visible-placement clock, five-second threshold, and pass/fail reporting for each platform. - [ ] T028 Document installation, explicit local model acquisition, defaults, privacy behavior, optional-context limitation, recovery command, and diagnostics in `README.md`.
## Parallel Opportunities
After T002, T003–T006 can proceed in parallel. After T006, T007–T010 can proceed in parallel. After T014, T015 and T016 can proceed in parallel. T024–T026 can proceed in parallel after T023.
## Implementation Strategy
MVP is T001–T014 and includes local Ollama cleanup as a mandatory stage. Do not add GUI/TUI, cloud, telemetry, databases, plugin/provider frameworks, or generalized backend abstractions.

"""Content-free readiness checks and the safe local dictation orchestration."""
from __future__ import annotations
import time from collections.abc import Callable, Sequence from dataclasses import dataclass from typing import Protocol
from dictate.config import Preferences from dictate.context import BoundedContext from dictate.platform.base import Capability, PlatformAdapter, TargetSnapshot from dictate.privacy import PrivacyError, validate_loopback_url from dictate.session import DictationSession, SessionState
class ReadinessBoundary(Protocol): def asr_ready(self, endpoint: str) -> Capability: ... def ollama_model_ready(self, endpoint: str, model: str) -> Capability: ... def microphone_ready(self, device: str) -> Capability: ... def trigger_ready(self, trigger: str) -> Capability: ... def placement_ready(self) -> Capability: ... def context_ready(self) -> Capability: ...
@dataclass(frozen=True) class ReadinessResult: required_failures: tuple[str, ...] limitations: tuple[str, ...]
@property def ready(self) -> bool: return not self.required_failures
def check_readiness(preferences: Preferences, boundary: ReadinessBoundary) -> ReadinessResult: """Check every required local capability without collecting user content.""" try: validate_loopback_url(preferences.asr_endpoint) validate_loopback_url(preferences.ollama_endpoint) except PrivacyError as error: return ReadinessResult((str(error),), ()) required = ( ("local ASR", boundary.asr_ready(preferences.asr_endpoint)), ("local Ollama model", boundary.ollama_model_ready(preferences.ollama_endpoint, preferences.ollama_model)), ("microphone", boundary.microphone_ready(preferences.microphone)), ("global trigger", boundary.trigger_ready(preferences.trigger)), ("safe text placement", boundary.placement_ready()), ) failures = tuple(f"{name}: {value.remediation or 'unavailable'}" for name, value in required if not value.available) context = boundary.context_ready() limitations = () if context.available else (f"destination context: {context.remediation or 'unavailable'}",) return ReadinessResult(failures, limitations)
class RecorderBoundary(Protocol): def start(self) -> None: ... def stop(self) -> bytes: ... def discard(self) -> None: ...
class ASRBoundary(Protocol): def start(self) -> None: ... def stop(self) -> None: ... def transcribe(self, pcm: bytes, terms: Sequence[str] = ()) -> str: ...
class CleanupBoundary(Protocol): def clean(self, transcript: str, style: str, terms: Sequence[str] = (), context: str | None = None) -> str: ...
class RecoveryStore: """One process-local result, destructively read and never persisted."""
def __init__(self, timeout_seconds: float = 60.0, clock: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic) -> None: self._timeout_seconds = timeout_seconds self._clock = clock self._result: str | None = None self._expires_at: float | None = None
def put(self, result: str) -> None: self.clear() self._result = result self._expires_at = self._clock() + self._timeout_seconds
def take(self) -> str | None: if self._expires_at is None or self._clock() >= self._expires_at: self.clear() return None result = self._result self.clear() return result
def clear(self) -> None: self._result = None self._expires_at = None
DEFAULT_RECOVERY = RecoveryStore()
class DictationService: """One active session: snapshot → RAM audio → ASR → Ollama → safe insert/recovery."""
def __init__( self, preferences: Preferences, platform: PlatformAdapter, recorder: RecorderBoundary, asr: ASRBoundary, cleanup: CleanupBoundary, *, recovery: RecoveryStore = DEFAULT_RECOVERY, status: Callable[[str], None] | None = None, terms_for_target: Callable[[TargetSnapshot], Sequence[str]] | None = None, ) -> None: self.preferences = preferences self.platform = platform self.recorder = recorder self.asr = asr self.cleanup = cleanup self.recovery = recovery self.status = status or (lambda _event: None) self.terms_for_target = terms_for_target or (lambda _target: ()) self.session = DictationSession() self._target: TargetSnapshot | None = None self._terms: tuple[str, ...] = ()
def start(self) -> None: self.asr.start() self.platform.start_hotkey(self.preferences.trigger, self.press, self.release)
def stop(self) -> None: try: self.platform.stop_hotkey() finally: try: if self.session.state is SessionState.RECORDING: try: self.recorder.stop() except Exception: pass finally: self.recorder.discard() elif self.session.state not in (SessionState.IDLE, SessionState.INSERTED, SessionState.RECOVERY, SessionState.FAILED): self.recorder.discard() finally: try: self.asr.stop() finally: self.recovery.clear() self._target = None if self.session.state not in (SessionState.IDLE, SessionState.INSERTED, SessionState.RECOVERY, SessionState.FAILED): self.session.fail() else: self.session.clear_content()
def press(self) -> None: if self.session.state is not SessionState.IDLE: self.status("dictation-busy") return target = self.platform.snapshot_target() if target is None: self.status("target-unavailable") return try: self._target = target self._terms = tuple(self.terms_for_target(target)) context_permission = getattr(self.platform, "context_permission", lambda: Capability(False))() if context_permission.available: try: raw_context = self.platform.read_context(target, self.preferences.context_limit) self.session.context = raw_context.render(self.preferences.context_limit) if isinstance(raw_context, BoundedContext) else (raw_context or "")[:self.preferences.context_limit] or None except Exception: self.session.context = None self.session.transition(SessionState.RECORDING) self.recorder.start() except Exception: self._fail("recording-unavailable")
def release(self) -> None: if self.session.state is not SessionState.RECORDING: return try: audio = self.recorder.stop() self.session.audio = audio if not audio: self._fail("empty-capture") return self.session.transition(SessionState.RECOGNIZING) transcript = self.asr.transcribe(audio, terms=self._terms) self.session.transcript = transcript self.session.transition(SessionState.CLEANING) output = self.cleanup.clean(transcript, self.preferences.style, terms=self._terms, context=self.session.context) self.session.output = output self.session.transition(SessionState.VALIDATING_TARGET) target = self._target if target is None or not self.platform.target_matches(target) or not self.platform.insert_text(target, output): self.recovery.put(output) self.session.transition(SessionState.RECOVERY) self.status("recovery-required") return self.session.transition(SessionState.INSERTED) self.status("inserted") except Exception: self._fail("local-processing-failed") finally: self._target = None self._terms = ()

"""Content-free readiness checks and the safe local dictation orchestration."""
from __future__ import annotations
import time from collections.abc import Callable, Sequence from dataclasses import dataclass from typing import Protocol
from dictate.config import Preferences from dictate.context import BoundedContext from dictate.platform.base import Capability, PlatformAdapter, TargetSnapshot from dictate.privacy import PrivacyError, validate_loopback_url from dictate.session import DictationSession, SessionState
class ReadinessBoundary(Protocol): def asr_ready(self, endpoint: str) -> Capability: ... def ollama_model_ready(self, endpoint: str, model: str) -> Capability: ... def microphone_ready(self, device: str) -> Capability: ... def trigger_ready(self, trigger: str) -> Capability: ... def placement_ready(self) -> Capability: ... def context_ready(self) -> Capability: ...
@dataclass(frozen=True) class ReadinessResult: required_failures: tuple[str, ...] limitations: tuple[str, ...]
@property def ready(self) -> bool: return not self.required_failures
@dataclass(frozen=True) class PlacementTiming: """Content-free timing from trigger release to terminal placement outcome."""
duration_ms: int outcome: str
@property def meets_five_second_target(self) -> bool: return self.outcome == "inserted" and self.duration_ms <= 5_000
def check_readiness(preferences: Preferences, boundary: ReadinessBoundary) -> ReadinessResult: """Check every required local capability without collecting user content.""" try: validate_loopback_url(preferences.asr_endpoint) validate_loopback_url(preferences.ollama_endpoint) except PrivacyError as error: return ReadinessResult((str(error),), ()) required = ( ("local ASR", boundary.asr_ready(preferences.asr_endpoint)), ("local Ollama model", boundary.ollama_model_ready(preferences.ollama_endpoint, preferences.ollama_model)), ("microphone", boundary.microphone_ready(preferences.microphone)), ("global trigger", boundary.trigger_ready(preferences.trigger)), ("safe text placement", boundary.placement_ready()), ) failures = tuple(f"{name}: {value.remediation or 'unavailable'}" for name, value in required if not value.available) context = boundary.context_ready() limitations = () if context.available else (f"destination context: {context.remediation or 'unavailable'}",) return ReadinessResult(failures, limitations)
class RecorderBoundary(Protocol): def start(self) -> None: ... def stop(self) -> bytes: ... def discard(self) -> None: ...
class ASRBoundary(Protocol): def start(self) -> None: ... def stop(self) -> None: ... def transcribe(self, pcm: bytes, terms: Sequence[str] = ()) -> str: ...
class CleanupBoundary(Protocol): def clean(self, transcript: str, style: str, terms: Sequence[str] = (), context: str | None = None) -> str: ...
class RecoveryStore: """One process-local result, destructively read and never persisted."""
def __init__(self, timeout_seconds: float = 60.0, clock: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic) -> None: self._timeout_seconds = timeout_seconds self._clock = clock self._result: str | None = None self._expires_at: float | None = None
def put(self, result: str) -> None: self.clear() self._result = result self._expires_at = self._clock() + self._timeout_seconds
def take(self) -> str | None: if self._expires_at is None or self._clock() >= self._expires_at: self.clear() return None result = self._result self.clear() return result
def clear(self) -> None: self._result = None self._expires_at = None
DEFAULT_RECOVERY = RecoveryStore()
class DictationService: """One active session: snapshot → RAM audio → ASR → Ollama → safe insert/recovery."""
def __init__( self, preferences: Preferences, platform: PlatformAdapter, recorder: RecorderBoundary, asr: ASRBoundary, cleanup: CleanupBoundary, *, recovery: RecoveryStore = DEFAULT_RECOVERY, status: Callable[[str], None] | None = None, terms_for_target: Callable[[TargetSnapshot], Sequence[str]] | None = None, clock: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic, timing_reporter: Callable[[PlacementTiming], None] | None = None, ) -> None: self.preferences = preferences self.platform = platform self.recorder = recorder self.asr = asr self.cleanup = cleanup self.recovery = recovery self.status = status or (lambda _event: None) self.terms_for_target = terms_for_target or (lambda _target: ()) self._clock = clock self._timing_reporter = timing_reporter or (lambda _timing: None) self.session = DictationSession() self._target: TargetSnapshot | None = None self._terms: tuple[str, ...] = ()
def start(self) -> None: self.asr.start() self.platform.start_hotkey(self.preferences.trigger, self.press, self.release)
def stop(self) -> None: try: self.platform.stop_hotkey() finally: try: if self.session.state is SessionState.RECORDING: try: self.recorder.stop() except Exception: pass finally: self.recorder.discard() elif self.session.state not in (SessionState.IDLE, SessionState.INSERTED, SessionState.RECOVERY, SessionState.FAILED): self.recorder.discard() finally: try: self.asr.stop() finally: self.recovery.clear() self._target = None if self.session.state not in (SessionState.IDLE, SessionState.INSERTED, SessionState.RECOVERY, SessionState.FAILED): self.session.fail() else: self.session.clear_content()
def press(self) -> None: if self.session.state is not SessionState.IDLE: self.status("dictation-busy") return target = self.platform.snapshot_target() if target is None: self.status("target-unavailable") return try: self._target = target self._terms = tuple(self.terms_for_target(target)) context_permission = getattr(self.platform, "context_permission", lambda: Capability(False))() if context_permission.available: try: raw_context = self.platform.read_context(target, self.preferences.context_limit) self.session.context = raw_context.render(self.preferences.context_limit) if isinstance(raw_context, BoundedContext) else (raw_context or "")[:self.preferences.context_limit] or None except Exception: self.session.context = None self.session.transition(SessionState.RECORDING) self.recorder.start() except Exception: self._fail("recording-unavailable")
def release(self) -> None: if self.session.state is not SessionState.RECORDING: return released_at = self._clock() outcome = "local-processing-failed" try: audio = self.recorder.stop() self.session.audio = audio if not audio: self._fail("empty-capture") outcome = "empty-capture" return self.session.transition(SessionState.RECOGNIZING) transcript = self.asr.transcribe(audio, terms=self._terms) self.session.transcript = transcript self.session.transition(SessionState.CLEANING) output = self.cleanup.clean(transcript, self.preferences.style, terms=self._terms, context=self.session.context) self.session.output = output self.session.transition(SessionState.VALIDATING_TARGET) target = self._target if target is None or not self.platform.target_matches(target) or not self.platform.insert_text(target, output): self.recovery.put(output) self.session.transition(SessionState.RECOVERY) self.status("recovery-required") outcome = "recovery-required" return self.session.transition(SessionState.INSERTED) self.status("inserted") outcome = "inserted" except Exception: self._fail("local-processing-failed") finally: duration_ms = max(0, round((self._clock() - released_at) * 1_000)) self._timing_reporter(PlacementTiming(duration_ms, outcome)) self._target = None self._terms = ()
def _fail(self, event: str) -> None: try: self.recorder.discard() except Exception: pass if self.session.state not in (SessionState.IDLE, SessionState.INSERTED, SessionState.RECOVERY, SessionState.FAILED): self.session.fail() else: self.session.clear_content() self._target = None self._terms = () self.status(event)

from __future__ import annotations
import unittest
from dictate.config import Preferences from dictate.platform.base import Capability, PlatformAdapter, TargetSnapshot from dictate.service import DictationService, RecoveryStore
PLATFORMS = ("macos", "windows", "linux")
class MatrixPlatform(PlatformAdapter): """Deterministic platform seam shared by every acceptance-matrix row."""
def __init__(self) -> None: self.active_target = TargetSnapshot("application", "window-a", "field") self.writes: list[TargetSnapshot] = [] self.callbacks: tuple[object, object] | None = None
def microphone_permission(self) -> Capability: return Capability(True) def trigger_permission(self) -> Capability: return Capability(True) def placement_permission(self) -> Capability: return Capability(True) def context_permission(self) -> Capability: return Capability(False, "grant platform accessibility permission") def snapshot_target(self) -> TargetSnapshot | None: return self.active_target def read_context(self, target: TargetSnapshot, limit: int) -> str | None: return None def target_matches(self, target: TargetSnapshot) -> bool: return target == self.active_target def insert_text(self, target: TargetSnapshot, text: str) -> bool: if not self.target_matches(target): return False self.writes.append(target) return True def start_hotkey(self, trigger: str, on_press: object, on_release: object) -> None: self.callbacks = (on_press, on_release) def stop_hotkey(self) -> None: self.callbacks = None def recovery_instruction(self) -> str: return "dictate serve --recover"
class Recorder: def start(self) -> None: pass def stop(self) -> bytes: return FIXED_SHORT_PCM def discard(self) -> None: pass
class ASR: def start(self) -> None: pass def stop(self) -> None: pass def transcribe(self, pcm: bytes, terms: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> str: return "fixture"
class Cleanup: def clean(self, transcript: str, style: str, terms: tuple[str, ...] = (), context: str | None = None) -> str: return "fixture"
# 100 ms of deterministic 16 kHz mono signed-16-bit silence, never user audio. FIXED_SHORT_PCM = b"\x00\x00" * 1_600
class PlatformMatrixAcceptanceTests(unittest.TestCase): def test_shared_contract_preserves_trigger_optional_context_and_safe_placement(self) -> None: for platform_name in PLATFORMS: with self.subTest(platform=platform_name): platform = MatrixPlatform() recovery = RecoveryStore() service = DictationService(Preferences(), platform, Recorder(), ASR(), Cleanup(), recovery=recovery)
service.start() self.assertIsNotNone(platform.callbacks) self.assertFalse(platform.context_permission().available) self.assertEqual("dictate serve --recover", platform.recovery_instruction())
service.press() platform.active_target = TargetSnapshot("application", "window-b", "field") service.release()
self.assertEqual([], platform.writes) self.assertEqual("fixture", recovery.take()) service.stop()
if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()
